options: How fast the number of steps grows when the input grows
How many seconds the code takes on your laptop
How much memory the file takes on disk
How many lines the function has
why: Seconds change with the computer. Steps and their growth do not. 10 times more items with O(n²) means about 100 times more steps.

q: A function with a loop inside a loop over the same list of n items is…
why: A loop inside a loop multiplies: n × n. Two loops one after the other are added: O(n) + O(n) is still O(n).

q: `for (const x of a) { if (a.includes(x + 1)) count++; }` is O(n²). Why?
options: `includes` is a hidden loop, so it is a loop inside a loop
why: `includes` walks the array, so it is O(n) per call. Put it inside a loop over n items and you get O(n²). A Set lookup is about one step.

q: At 100,000 items, the nested-loop duplicate check took about 3,899 ms and the Set version about 8 ms. What does the Set version cost in return?
why: Most speed-ups spend memory. The Set can hold every item, so the space is O(n). Always say both the time and the space.

q: Which line hides a loop and makes a loop around it O(n²)?
why: `shift` moves every item one place left: O(n) per call. 100,000 shifts took about 1,049 ms; with a head index it took 0.2 ms.

q: The interviewer asks for a solution. What do you say first?
options: Nothing until you have the best answer
The simple brute force, with its cost, then what repeats and how to improve it
That you cannot solve it without a hint
Only the final O(n) solution, no brute force
why: Brute force first, say its cost, find the repeated work, improve, and say the new cost. Saying the simple way is a good start, not a failure.
